Emphasis is a circle drawn in one open loop, or the red seal placed beside the point
Steps are shown as separate small scenes along a scroll, separated by mist, not as a list
sound: Soft dry brush swish matching each stroke, pitch following its speed
Low muted wooden knock or distant bell tone when a scene arrives
Small damp thud for the seal press
Very quiet airy bed, nothing rhythmic
avoid: Bright or many colours; anything beyond ink greys and the single red seal
Hard vector outlines, drop shadows, gradients that look digital
Crowded frames with no empty paper

name: Stained Glass
description: A cathedral window: jewel-coloured glass pieces held by thick dark lead lines, lit from behind so colours glow and light spills onto the floor.
suits: Suits grand, ceremonial, historical or symbolic stories and big single ideas; poor for fine detail, small text, precise charts or casual, playful tones.
look: The frame is split into many irregular glass pieces, each filled with one flat jewel colour, separated by thick near-black lead lines with rounded joints
Pieces carry a mottled hand-made variation: faint swirls, tiny bubbles, streaks and slightly lighter patches where the glass is thinner
Subjects are drawn in bold simplified shapes, outlined by lead, with fine dark paint hatching inside for faces, folds and feathers
Pointed arch or round-top frame with a stone border; the scene sits inside it, with a patterned border band of repeating small glass pieces
Light shines through from behind: colour centres are bright, edges near the lead are deeper, and rays fan outward
Text sits in a gothic blackletter for headings, in dark paint on a pale glass banner, with a plainer serif for small words
Distinct from Paper Layers and Bauhaus: shapes interlock with no gaps and no overlap, and everything glows
finish: A bright back-light glow bleeding a little past each piece's lead edge, medium strength
Soft shafts of coloured light cast diagonally onto a dark stone floor or wall, drifting slowly
Fine pitted glass texture and tiny streaks over each pane, low strength
Dark corner falloff so the window feels set in a dim room
motion: Lead lines draw on first, growing along their path, then glass pieces fill with colour one at a time from dark to bright
Pieces may light up in a quick ripple from the centre outward, like sun reaching the window
Beats change by the window dimming to black then relighting as a new window, or by panes flipping colour
Pace is stately; slow light drift and gentle shimmer rather than quick moves
Nothing moves out of its lead cell; objects change by recolouring, not sliding
explaining: Labels are lettered on pale glass banners curling across the scene, in dark paint
Arrows are pointed lead strips or rays of coloured light travelling between panes
Numbers are set big inside a round glass medallion, framed by a ring of small beads
Emphasis is a single pane lit far brighter than its neighbours, with a halo of rays
Steps are separate panels of one tall window, read from bottom to top, each with its own medallion
sound: Clear glass chime or crystal ping as each pane lights
Low sustained choir-like pad or organ-like drone under the whole piece
Soft tinkle of glass when pieces shift
avoid: Thin lines, gradients across several panes, or soft shadows inside a pane
Pastel or neon colours; only deep jewel tones
Small body text on busy glass

name: Folded Paper
description: Crisp low-poly shapes folded from a single sheet of coloured paper: sharp creases, flat facets lit differently, and parts that unfold into one another.
suits: Suits transformations, structure, product shape, steps that build on each other and tidy modern topics; poor for organic, messy, emotional or very text-heavy subjects.
look: Everything is made of flat triangles and quadrilaterals meeting at sharp creases, each facet filled with its own tone so the object reads as a folded solid
Each facet is a slightly lighter or darker version of one base colour, depending on how it faces a light from the upper left
Thin faint crease lines run along every fold; edges have a hairline highlight on the lit side
A calm, matte, slightly warm light-grey backdrop with a soft contact shadow under every model, pooling wider as the model lifts
Subjects are simple animals, boxes, arrows, birds, cranes or abstract gems built from few facets; never rounded
Occasional flat sheets with a diagonal fold-line and a visible paper grain on both faces, one side a different colour from the other
Text is clean geometric sans, placed on a flat paper tab or on the backdrop, never on folded facets
Distinct from Paper Layers: those are flat stacked cutouts, this is faceted folding with a single sheet turning into a form
finish: Fine paper fibre grain on every facet, very light
Soft shadow under each model and a faint darker line inside every crease, medium
A gentle top-left light wash on the backdrop, nothing dramatic
motion: A flat square sheet appears, then folds step by step: corners swing over on their crease lines with a slight perspective squash
Models rotate a few degrees slowly to show facets catching light
Beats change by one object folding itself flat then folding into the next shape
Pace is deliberate and precise, with a small settle at the end of each fold
Things unfold to reveal text on the inner face
explaining: Labels sit on small folded tabs or flags, with a dotted fold line to the subject
Arrows are folded paper arrows or dashed fold lines with a small curved arrow showing the flip direction
Numbers are printed large on a flat white card that folds out from behind the model
Emphasis lifts a facet or whole model higher, with a larger shadow, while the rest stays flat
Steps follow an origami diagram habit: numbered squares showing each fold in sequence
sound: Short crisp paper fold snap or crease with each fold
Dry soft paper slide when a sheet moves
Light airy tick as a step lands
Quiet minimal tone bed, nothing heavy
avoid: Curves and smooth gradients; faceted flat tones only
Heavy outlines, glossy highlights or realistic wood or cloth textures
Unfolded clutter with no clear light direction

name: Chalkboard Lesson
description: White and pastel chalk on a dark green-black classroom board, with smudged ghosts of old writing, dusty lines and a lesson-like, teacherly pace.
suits: Suits teaching, step-by-step logic, sums, history and anything that should feel like being taught; weak for glossy products, luxury or very modern tech themes.
look: A dark slate board with a soft cloudy lighter patch where the wiper passed, faint ghost writing barely visible, and a wooden frame with a chalk ledge at the bottom
Chalk lines are slightly broken, uneven in width and dusty at the edge, with tiny gaps where the stick skipped over the board
Lettering is a casual teacher's hand in white, with one or two pastel colours for key parts; letters lean slightly and wander off the baseline
Drawings are quick, simple and a bit wobbly: boxes, stick figures, circles with shaded hatching, rough graphs with axes and tick marks
Underlines, boxes and circles are drawn twice, with a slight overshoot where the strokes meet
Fill is done by hatching and scribbled shading in diagonal strokes, never solid
A small eraser smudge or hand-wipe patch sometimes removes part of the content
Distinct from Whiteboard: the board is dark, strokes are dusty and soft, and rubbed-out areas leave ghosts
finish: Chalk grain: each stroke is multiplied by a rough speckle so it looks dusty and thin in places, strong
Soft white dust haze around heavy strokes, low strength
Wipe smears across the board that never fully clean it, medium
Slight uneven top lighting, brighter in the middle
motion: Everything is written live: strokes advance along their path at hand speed, with a tiny pause between letters and a longer pause between lines
Underlines and circles are drawn after the thing they mark, with a quick stroke
A hand-wipe sweeps across to clear a section, leaving a soft ghost, before the next lesson step starts
Pace is classroom steady, never hurried, with beats separated by a short pause
No bouncing; things only appear by being drawn or fade by being rubbed out
explaining: Labels are written next to the thing with a short chalk line, in a different colour from the object
Arrows are loose hand-drawn lines with a two-stroke head, sometimes curved around a step
Numbers are written big, with a sum written beneath and underlined twice for the answer
Emphasis is a circled word, double underline or a coloured chalk star in the margin
Steps are numbered down the left side like a worked lesson, each crossed off or ticked afterward
sound: Scratchy chalk strokes whose pitch follows speed
Tap of chalk placed on the ledge or a tapping dot
Soft felt eraser swish for wipes
Optional small knock for a finished answer
avoid: Clean vector lines or perfect typography
Bright saturated fills; chalk colours are pastel and dusty
A pure black or clean-looking board

name: Blueprint
description: A technical drawing in pale lines on deep cyan-blue paper: grid, dimensions, callouts and a title block, drawn like an engineer's plan.
suits: Suits systems, architecture, processes, specs and how-it-is-built explanations with a precise, engineered tone; poor for emotional stories or anything that needs colour and warmth.
look: Deep blue sheet with a fine grid of thin pale lines, every fifth line a little stronger, and a thin border frame with tick marks and grid letters on the edges
All drawing is thin white-blue line work with no fills, except sparse diagonal hatching to show cut surfaces
Objects are shown as plan and side views, exploded parts and dashed hidden lines, with centre lines made of long-short dashes
Dimension lines run outside the object with small end arrows, extension ticks and a value written mid-line
A title block sits in the lower right: boxed cells with sheet name, scale, date and a revision list in tiny capital letters
Circled numbers tag parts and link to a list in the margin; small notes in slanted capitals point with leader lines
Text is monospaced uppercase with wide spacing; nothing is rounded or soft
Distinct from Xray Scan: this is a drafted line plan on paper, not a glowing translucent scan, and has no glow
finish: Subtle paper tone: a slightly lighter centre and darker corners, low
Fine blueprint-paper mottling and faint fold creases, very low
A tiny line-weight wobble and a slight bleed on thick lines so they feel printed, low strength
motion: Lines are drafted on: each line extends from one end to the other at a steady speed, like a plotter
Grid and frame appear first, then the object outlines, then dimensions and notes
Dimension arrows slide out from the middle to the ends, and the value types in
Beats change by a new sheet sliding in or the current drawing zooming into a detail circle
Pace is measured and exact with no bounce; short pauses after each group of lines
explaining: Labels are small capital notes joined by a leader line with a dot at the target
Arrows are dimension arrows and flow arrows with simple, narrow closed heads
Numbers are shown in dimension lines and in a quantity table with ruled rows, set in mono
Emphasis is the only place to use the yellow: a bracket or a revision cloud of scalloped arcs around a part
Steps are numbered sheets or numbered circle tags that follow an assembly order
sound: Fast thin ticking as lines are drawn, like a plotter pen
Short digital tick or type blip for numbers and notes
Low soft hum bed, nothing melodic
A small rubber-stamp thump for approved or final marks
avoid: Filled colour areas, shadows or glows
Rounded casual handwriting
More than one accent colour

name: Notebook Doodle
description: Blue ballpoint pen scribbled on ruled school paper: wobbly pressure-varied lines, dense cross-hatched shading and fat bubble letters, with a red pen for corrections.
suits: Good for friendly, casual explanations of ideas, processes and comparisons, told like a clever student's margin notes; poor for polished corporate, luxury or very serious subjects.
look: Page is off-white lined paper with pale blue horizontal rules, a single faint red margin line down the left, and a few punched holes or a ragged spiral edge; the whole scene is one long page the view slides along
Everything is drawn with one blue ballpoint line: slightly shaky, thicker where the pen presses and thinner on quick flicks, with a small dark blob where each stroke begins
Shadows and darks are built from layers of thin parallel hatching, then a second set at a crossing angle; the denser the hatching, the darker the area, with no filled grey
Headings are fat bubble letters: hollow outlined letters with a hatched shadow offset down and right, sometimes with tiny stars or lines beside them
Boxes and labels are hand-ruled rectangles with wobbly corners and a hatched drop shadow; body text is neat but uneven joined-up handwriting in blue
Margins and gaps fill with compulsive little doodles (spirals, stars, zigzags, tiny faces) that get traced over several times until the line looks dark and furry
A red pen is used only for judgment: ticks, crosses, circles and underlines; a second faint pencil grey may be used for a rough first sketch under the ink
finish: Paper grain: fine warm speckle and slight fibre across the page, light (about 5 percent)
Faint uneven shading toward the page edges and a soft shadow in the spiral or fold area, subtle
Ink wobble: every line is displaced by a tiny low-frequency jitter so no stroke is perfectly straight
A slight embossed groove look on a few heavy strokes where the pen pressed through, very subtle
motion: Lines are drawn on stroke by stroke in the order a hand would make them, the pen tip always at the end of the visible line
Shading arrives in passes: first an outline, then one hatch direction, then the crossing direction, each pass taking a beat
The view scrolls along the page like a hand moving the notebook, easing to rest on each new piece of work
New topics start further down or on a turned page; old doodles stay behind as a record
Pace is brisk but scribbly, with tiny pauses where the pen would lift
explaining: Labels are written beside the thing with a short wobbly leader line, or inside a ruled box with a hatched shadow
Arrows are hand-drawn curved lines with a two-stroke open head, drawn on in the direction of flow
Numbers are written large as bubble numerals; a changed number is struck through in red and rewritten beside it
Wrong guesses get a red cross and a red correction; right answers get a tick and an underline
Emphasis is a loose double circle in red pen, or heavy underlining with a few radiating tick marks
Steps are numbered down the page like a worked exercise
sound: Scratchy pen on paper while any line draws, rising in pitch and length with the stroke
Dry soft thud for a box landing and a quick click for the pen tap
A short paper rustle on page scrolls and turns
A bright little tick chime on a correct answer, a flat low scrape on a red cross
avoid: Clean digital vector lines or perfectly straight rules and circles
Fills of flat colour, gradients or any colour beyond blue, red and a trace of grey
Fonts that look typeset instead of handwritten, outside the bubble headings

name: Noir
description: A black-and-white forties crime-picture look: hard slashes of light and deep shadow, heavy film grain, and captions and stamps styled like an old newsreel.
suits: Good for mysteries, investigations, risk, money, security and any story told as a case being cracked; poor for cheerful, soft or colourful topics.
look: Pure monochrome from near-black to warm bright white, with very deep shadows covering most of the frame and a few hard, bright shapes of light
Light arrives as diagonal bars (as through window blinds) cast across walls and subjects, with crisp edges and slightly tilted angles that sway very slowly
Subjects are mostly silhouettes or half-lit forms, edged by a thin bright rim where a light source sits behind them
Hanging haze or smoke drifts through the beams, visible only where light catches it
Scene changes use film language: a closing iris, a wipe, a clock sweep, or a spinning newspaper front page that lands with a headline
Labels look like old paper placards and typewriter slips: off-white card, black type, thin double border, sometimes a stamped case number
Big titles are tall condensed capitals in off-white, with a faint glow; supporting text is typewriter type
finish: Heavy film grain on every frame, re-rolled each frame, strong (about 15 percent)
Gate weave: the whole picture drifts a pixel or two and rotates a hair, plus brightness flicker like a projector, moderate
Dust specks, hairs and thin vertical scratches that appear for a frame or two, light but regular
Dark vignette pulling the corners nearly black, strong
Slight softness and glow on bright areas, as if shot on old stock
motion: Bars of light drift and sway slowly, and the haze curls upward
Elements fade up out of darkness, brightest parts first, rather than popping on
Titles and captions arrive word by word with a small flicker
Beats are joined by iris, wipe and clock-sweep transitions; headlines spin in for topic changes
Camera moves are slow pushes in with a faint handheld tremble
explaining: Labels are typed on placards that slide in and rest slightly crooked, like case-file or booking cards
Arrows are plain bright white newsreel arrows drawn on with a thin steady line
Numbers roll on a mechanical counter, digits ticking like a cash register or odometer
For emphasis an inked stamp thumps onto the frame at a slant, and the whole picture jolts slightly
Steps appear as a montage of short headline cards, each with a brief title and one line
sound: Low warm room tone with a faint projector whirr under everything
Typewriter keys while text is typed
Heavy thud for a stamp, with a short dry reverb
Soft mechanical ticks for a rolling counter; a muted brass sting for a reveal
avoid: Colour, or soft evenly lit scenes with no hard shadow
Clean digital sharpness with no grain or weave
Cartoon shapes or rounded friendly fonts
Confusing with Shadow Theatre: here it is photographic light and shade on forms, not flat cut-out silhouettes on a lit screen

name: Neon Sign
description: Glowing bent-glass neon tubes on a dark wet-night brick wall, with coloured light spilling over the bricks and smearing in puddles below.
suits: Good for nightlife, retail, tech, music and punchy lists of ideas; poor for daylight, quiet or text-heavy technical material.
look: Dark brick wall in near-black red-brown with visible courses of bricks and mortar lines, lit only by the signs
Every drawn thing is a single continuous glass tube: bright white-hot core line, a tinted colour band around it, then a wide soft halo
Letters are bent in a thin single-line script or rounded sans, with unlit tube sections painted out in dull dark grey where the glass runs behind
Small metal clips, brackets and end caps hold each tube to the wall, with a short cable running off
Coloured light washes across nearby bricks and pools in a wet pavement strip at the bottom, with a blurred, rippling mirror image of the signs
Sign backing plates or frames are matt black metal with a thin lit outline tube
Pink, cyan, amber and a warning red are the tube colours; never more than three lit at once
finish: Additive glow: each tube is blurred twice at different widths and added over the wall, strong
Light wash on bricks: soft coloured gradient following each sign, medium
Wet reflection: a flipped, blurred, rippled copy below the horizon line, faded, with ripples jittering as drops land
Fine grain and a light vignette, subtle
Slow flicker: a tiny brightness hum on all tubes, with one or two letters flickering harder
motion: Signs light up tube by tube and letter by letter with a stuttering buzz: dark, a weak flash, dark, then full light
One letter keeps failing and flickering through the whole scene
The view whip-pans sideways along the wall to the next sign, with a quick blur, and settles with a slight overshoot
Drops fall into the puddle and send rings through the reflection
Pace is rhythmic, with each beat being a new sign
explaining: Each point gets its own sign on the wall; labels are neon words, short and lowercase or capitals
Arrows are chains of short tube segments that light one after another toward the target, like chase bulbs
Numbers are neon digits; when a value changes the old digits snap dark and new ones buzz on
Emphasis is a red tube that blinks, ringed by a lit circle or burst of rays
Comparisons are two signs in different colours side by side
sound: Low electrical hum bed, with a rise in loudness when more tubes are on
Sharp crackle and buzz as each tube ignites, with a short zap
Soft rain drips and splashes on the puddle
Relay clack for a sign switching off, bright chime for a resolve
avoid: Solid filled letters or flat daylight colours
Glow with no white core, or a halo so wide that the tube shape is lost
Confusing with Neon Circuit: here it is physical glass on brick in a wet street, not a digital grid and traces

name: Manga Panel
description: A black-and-white Japanese comic page: slanted panels, brush-ink lines, burst lines for impact, screentone dots and bold sound-effect lettering.
suits: Good for dramatic cause and effect, challenges, power-ups and energetic how-it-works stories; poor for calm reference material and dense text.
look: White page with thick black panel borders cut at slanted angles and separated by even white gutters; panels sometimes overlap or burst past their frame
Line art is brush ink: tapered at both ends, thick on shadow sides, hair-thin for fine detail, with confident contours
Tone comes from fine screentone: regular dot grids of different density laid in flat areas and gradients, plus solid black fills for deep shadow
Focus lines: dense black strokes radiating from or converging on a point, with white gaps, behind important moments or speed
Sound-effect words are huge, jagged, hand-cut letters (in Japanese-style kana or bold Latin) with a thick white outline knocked out around them, placed across panel edges
Speech balloons are hand-drawn white ovals with a small tail; narration sits in rectangular boxes with square corners
Small emotion marks (sweat drops, sparks, cross-shaped veins) accent reactions
finish: Screentone dot screens that stay fixed to the page while shapes move over them, medium
Slight paper grain and off-white page tint, subtle
Ink edge roughness: a tiny wobble on lines, light
Brief high-contrast flash, black or white, on impact beats
motion: Panels drop in one or two at a time with a quick zoom, and the whole page shakes a little as each lands

name: Isometric Diorama
